claim: Many cancers overexpress one or more of the six human pro-survival BCL2 family proteins to evade apoptosis.
source: Many cancers overexpress one or more of the six human pro-survival BCL2 family proteins to evade apoptosis.
evidence: This is a general statement about cancer biology supported by established scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: Each computationally designed inhibitor binds its target with high picomolar to low nanomolar affinity.
source: Following in vitro optimization, each inhibitor binds its target with high picomolar to low nanomolar affinity and at least 300-fold specificity.
evidence: Binding affinities were measured experimentally using biolayer interferometry as shown in Figure 2.

claim: Each computationally designed inhibitor exhibits at least 300-fold specificity for its target.
source: Following in vitro optimization, each inhibitor binds its target with high picomolar to low nanomolar affinity and at least 300-fold specificity.
evidence: Specificity was measured experimentally using biolayer interferometry comparing binding to target versus off-target BCL2 proteins.

claim: Expression of the designed inhibitors in human cancer cell lines revealed unique dependencies on BCL2 proteins for survival which could not be inferred from other BCL2 profiling methods.
source: Expression of the designed inhibitors in human cancer cell lines revealed unique dependencies on BCL2 proteins for survival which could not be inferred from other BCL2 profiling methods.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from cell viability assays in multiple cancer cell lines as shown in Figures 7-9.

claim: Pro-apoptotic effector proteins Bak and Bax have four distinct BH motifs and homo-oligomerize upon activation to form pores in the mitochondrial outer membrane.
source: Pro-apoptotic effector proteins Bak and Bax have four distinct BH motifs and homo-oligomerize upon activation to form pores in the mitochondrial outer membrane, committing the cell to apoptosis.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the BCL2 family protein structure and function.

claim: There are six human pro-survival BCL2 homologs: Bcl-2, Bcl-xL, Bcl-w, Mcl-1, Bfl-1 and Bcl-B.
source: Pro-survival homologs (six in humans: Bcl-2, Bcl-xL, Bcl-w, Mcl-1, Bfl-1 and Bcl-B) are structurally similar, but oppose apoptosis by binding and inhibiting Bak and Bax, as well as sequestering pro-apoptotic BH3-only proteins (BOPs).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the BCL2 family proteins.

claim: Pro-survival BCL2 homologs oppose apoptosis by binding and inhibiting Bak and Bax.
source: Pro-survival homologs (six in humans: Bcl-2, Bcl-xL, Bcl-w, Mcl-1, Bfl-1 and Bcl-B) are structurally similar, but oppose apoptosis by binding and inhibiting Bak and Bax, as well as sequestering pro-apoptotic BH3-only proteins (BOPs).
evidence: This is established knowledge about BCL2 protein function.

claim: Pro-survival BCL2 homologs oppose apoptosis by sequestering pro-apoptotic BH3-only proteins.
source: Pro-survival homologs (six in humans: Bcl-2, Bcl-xL, Bcl-w, Mcl-1, Bfl-1 and Bcl-B) are structurally similar, but oppose apoptosis by binding and inhibiting Bak and Bax, as well as sequestering pro-apoptotic BH3-only proteins (BOPs).
evidence: This is established knowledge about BCL2 protein function.

claim: BOPs can activate effectors directly through transient binding interactions.
source: BOPs can also activate effectors directly through transient binding interactions (Dai et al., 2011; Kim et al., 2009; Walensky et al., 2006) or indirectly by binding pro-survival proteins and out-competing bound effectors (Ku et al., 2011; Willis et al., 2007) or other direct activator BOPs (Kuwana et al., 2005; Letai et al., 2002; Figure 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: BOPs can activate effectors indirectly by binding pro-survival proteins and out-competing bound effectors.
source: BOPs can also activate effectors directly through transient binding interactions (Dai et al., 2011; Kim et al., 2009; Walensky et al., 2006) or indirectly by binding pro-survival proteins and out-competing bound effectors (Ku et al., 2011; Willis et al., 2007) or other direct activator BOPs (Kuwana et al., 2005; Letai et al., 2002; Figure 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Interactions between BCL2 members are mediated by an amphipathic, helical BH3 motif that recognizes a conserved hydrophobic cleft present in the effectors and pro-survival proteins.
source: Interactions between BCL2 members are mediated by an amphipathic, helical BH3 motif that recognizes a conserved hydrophobic cleft present in the effectors and pro-survival proteins.
evidence: This is established knowledge about BCL2 protein interactions.

claim: The small molecule ABT-737 targets Bcl-2, Bcl-xL and Bcl-w.
source: For example, the small molecule ABT-737 (and related ABT-263) targeting Bcl-2, Bcl-xL and Bcl-w exhibits dose-limiting thrombocytopenia in treating Bcl-2-dependent chronic lymphocytic leukemia due to excessive inhibition of Bcl-xL, which has a role in platelet development (Mason et al., 2007; Roberts et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: ABT-737 exhibits dose-limiting thrombocytopenia in treating Bcl-2-dependent chronic lymphocytic leukemia due to excessive inhibition of Bcl-xL.
source: For example, the small molecule ABT-737 (and related ABT-263) targeting Bcl-2, Bcl-xL and Bcl-w exhibits dose-limiting thrombocytopenia in treating Bcl-2-dependent chronic lymphocytic leukemia due to excessive inhibition of Bcl-xL, which has a role in platelet development (Mason et al., 2007; Roberts et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Bcl-xL has a role in platelet development.
source: For example, the small molecule ABT-737 (and related ABT-263) targeting Bcl-2, Bcl-xL and Bcl-w exhibits dose-limiting thrombocytopenia in treating Bcl-2-dependent chronic lymphocytic leukemia due to excessive inhibition of Bcl-xL, which has a role in platelet development (Mason et al., 2007; Roberts et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: BCL2 profiling using natural BOPs, BH3-mimicking peptides or small molecules is complicated by their low specificity.
source: BCL2 profiling using natural BOPs, BH3-mimicking peptides or small molecules is complicated by their low specificity (Certo et al., 2006; Chen et al., 2005; DeBartolo et al., 2012; London et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Designed peptides and small molecules have achieved high affinity and excellent specificity for Bcl-2.
source: Designed peptides and small molecules have achieved high affinity and excellent specificity for Bcl-2 (Souers et al., 2013), Bcl-xL (Leverson et al., 2015a), Mcl-1 (Lee et al., 2008; Foight et al., 2014; Leverson et al., 2015b), and Bfl-1 (Dutta et al., 2013), and highly specific small molecule inhibitors of Bcl-2 and Bcl-xL (ABT-199 and A-1155463) have defined the dependency of ABT-263-sensitive cancer cell lines on Bcl-2, Bcl-xL or both (Leverson et al., 2015a).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Designed peptides and small molecules have achieved high affinity and excellent specificity for Bcl-xL.
source: Designed peptides and small molecules have achieved high affinity and excellent specificity for Bcl-2 (Souers et al., 2013), Bcl-xL (Leverson et al., 2015a), Mcl-1 (Lee et al., 2008; Foight et al., 2014; Leverson et al., 2015b), and Bfl-1 (Dutta et al., 2013), and highly specific small molecule inhibitors of Bcl-2 and Bcl-xL (ABT-199 and A-1155463) have defined the dependency of ABT-263-sensitive cancer cell lines on Bcl-2, Bcl-xL or both (Leverson et al., 2015a).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Designed peptides and small molecules have achieved high affinity and excellent specificity for Mcl-1.
source: Designed peptides and small molecules have achieved high affinity and excellent specificity for Bcl-2 (Souers et al., 2013), Bcl-xL (Leverson et al., 2015a), Mcl-1 (Lee et al., 2008; Foight et al., 2014; Leverson et al., 2015b), and Bfl-1 (Dutta et al., 2013), and highly specific small molecule inhibitors of Bcl-2 and Bcl-xL (ABT-199 and A-1155463) have defined the dependency of ABT-263-sensitive cancer cell lines on Bcl-2, Bcl-xL or both (Leverson et al., 2015a).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Designed peptides and small molecules have achieved high affinity and excellent specificity for Bfl-1.
source: Designed peptides and small molecules have achieved high affinity and excellent specificity for Bcl-2 (Souers et al., 2013), Bcl-xL (Leverson et al., 2015a), Mcl-1 (Lee et al., 2008; Foight et al., 2014; Leverson et al., 2015b), and Bfl-1 (Dutta et al., 2013), and highly specific small molecule inhibitors of Bcl-2 and Bcl-xL (ABT-199 and A-1155463) have defined the dependency of ABT-263-sensitive cancer cell lines on Bcl-2, Bcl-xL or both (Leverson et al., 2015a).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: There are currently no highly specific inhibitors for Bcl-w and Bcl-B.
source: However, there are currently no highly specific inhibitors for Bcl-w and Bcl-B, and hence general mechanistic aspects of apoptotic regulation remain unclear.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of the field at the time of publication.

claim: BINDI is a de novo designed protein inhibitor of BHRF1, an Epstein-Barr viral BCL2 homolog.
source: We recently described a de novo designed protein inhibitor of BHRF1, an Epstein-Barr viral BCL2 homolog. The three helix bundle protein, called BINDI, is complementary to the canonical BH3-binding groove of BHRF1.
evidence: This refers to previously published work by the authors.

claim: BINDI consists of a central BH3-like motif and two additional helices that both stabilize the BH3-motif and provide extra contacts for high affinity and specific binding.
source: BINDI consists of a central BH3-like motif and two additional helices that both stabilize the BH3-motif and provide extra contacts for high affinity and specific binding (PDB 4OYD; Procko et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work and structural data.

claim: Pro-survival BCL2 homologs share 40–60% sequence similarity between any two members.
source: Pro-survival BCL2 homologs share similar sequences (40–60% similarity between any two) and structures (approximately 3 Å RMSD), and hence achieving specific binding for each one is a challenging problem.
evidence: This is a quantitative statement about sequence similarity that can be verified from sequence databases.

claim: Pro-survival BCL2 homologs have structures with approximately 3 Å RMSD.
source: Pro-survival BCL2 homologs share similar sequences (40–60% similarity between any two) and structures (approximately 3 Å RMSD), and hence achieving specific binding for each one is a challenging problem.
evidence: This is a quantitative statement about structural similarity that can be verified from structural databases.

claim: 2-CDP06 bound Bcl-2 with highest affinity among initial designs.
source: 2-CDP06 (for Bcl-2-targeting Computationally Designed Protein), X-CDP07 (Bcl-xL), M-CDP04 (Mcl-1), and F-CDP01 (Bfl-1) bound their intended targets with highest affinity, while the affinity of B-CDP01 to its intended target Bcl-B was second only to Mcl-1 (Figure 2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: This is supported by experimental binding data shown in Figure 2.

claim: X-CDP07 bound Bcl-xL with highest affinity among initial designs.
source: 2-CDP06 (for Bcl-2-targeting Computationally Designed Protein), X-CDP07 (Bcl-xL), M-CDP04 (Mcl-1), and F-CDP01 (Bfl-1) bound their intended targets with highest affinity, while the affinity of B-CDP01 to its intended target Bcl-B was second only to Mcl-1 (Figure 2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: This is supported by experimental binding data shown in Figure 2.

claim: M-CDP04 bound Mcl-1 with highest affinity among initial designs.
source: 2-CDP06 (for Bcl-2-targeting Computationally Designed Protein), X-CDP07 (Bcl-xL), M-CDP04 (Mcl-1), and F-CDP01 (Bfl-1) bound their intended targets with highest affinity, while the affinity of B-CDP01 to its intended target Bcl-B was second only to Mcl-1 (Figure 2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: This is supported by experimental binding data shown in Figure 2.

claim: F-CDP01 bound Bfl-1 with highest affinity among initial designs.
source: 2-CDP06 (for Bcl-2-targeting Computationally Designed Protein), X-CDP07 (Bcl-xL), M-CDP04 (Mcl-1), and F-CDP01 (Bfl-1) bound their intended targets with highest affinity, while the affinity of B-CDP01 to its intended target Bcl-B was second only to Mcl-1 (Figure 2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: This is supported by experimental binding data shown in Figure 2.

claim: B-CDP01's affinity to Bcl-B was second only to Mcl-1.
source: 2-CDP06 (for Bcl-2-targeting Computationally Designed Protein), X-CDP07 (Bcl-xL), M-CDP04 (Mcl-1), and F-CDP01 (Bfl-1) bound their intended targets with highest affinity, while the affinity of B-CDP01 to its intended target Bcl-B was second only to Mcl-1 (Figure 2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: This is supported by experimental binding data shown in Figure 2.

claim: Initial Bcl-w-targeting designs did not bind Bcl-w or any other BCL2 protein.
source: Initial Bcl-w-targeting designs, however, did not bind Bcl-w or any other BCL2 protein, likely because the designs were based on the crystal structure of Bcl-w bound to a ligand that is not BH3-like (PDB 4K5A), unlike successful designs that were based on BH3-liganded structures (Supplementary file 1A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental binding data and inference about the cause.

claim: W-CDP03 bound Bcl-w with nanomolar affinity and moderate specificity.
source: Design W-CDP03 was the most specific, binding Bcl-w with nanomolar affinity and moderate specificity (Figure 2C, Figure 2—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: This is supported by experimental binding data shown in Figure 2.

claim: The location of the BH3-like motif in W-CDP03 is shifted by one α-helical turn relative to BINDI.
source: Notably, the location of the BH3-like motif in W-CDP03 is shifted by one α-helical turn relative to BINDI, perhaps to better accommodate the Bcl-w surface (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D and E).
evidence: This is supported by structural analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D and E.

claim: M-CDP04 (αMCL1) was highly specific for Mcl-1 and bound with picomolar affinity.
source: One design, M-CDP04 (subsequently called αMCL1, or anti-Mcl-1), was highly specific for Mcl-1 and bound with picomolar affinity.
evidence: This is supported by experimental binding data shown in Figure 2.

claim: The crystal structure of the αMCL1•Mcl-1 complex was determined at 2.75 Å resolution.
source: The crystal structure of the αMCL1•Mcl-1 complex at 2.75 Å resolution reveals how high affinity and specificity were achieved (Figure 3, Supplementary file 1C).
evidence: This is experimental structural data deposited in the PDB.

claim: When Mcl-1 in the design model is superimposed on Mcl-1 in the crystal structure, αMCL1 crystal and design models closely align with 2.1 Å average RMSD.
source: When Mcl-1 in the design model is superimposed on Mcl-1 in the crystal structure, αMCL1 crystal and design models closely align, highlighting the accuracy of our design calculations (2.1 Å average RMSD among the six separate complexes observed in the asymmetric unit; the N-terminal end of αMCL1 in the crystal structure lying slightly closer to Mcl-1 than in the design).
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison of the design model to the crystal structure.

claim: αMCL1 expands the classic BH3 interface by 534 Å².
source: These extra contacts, combined with those made by the peripheral helices, expand the classic BH3 interface by 534 Å2 (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from the crystal structure shown in Figure 3B.

claim: For all CDPs, nearly all designed residues have enrichment ratios very close to the maximum, on average deviating by 2.2.
source: For all CDPs, nearly all designed residues have enrichment ratios very close to the maximum (Figure 5A, Figure 5—figure supplement 1B), on average deviating by 2.2 (2.2-fold worse enrichment) while the average deviation per position is 4.1 (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is a quantitative analysis of deep sequencing data shown in Figure 5.

claim: The average deviation per position in enrichment ratios is 4.1.
source: For all CDPs, nearly all designed residues have enrichment ratios very close to the maximum (Figure 5A, Figure 5—figure supplement 1B), on average deviating by 2.2 (2.2-fold worse enrichment) while the average deviation per position is 4.1 (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is a quantitative analysis of deep sequencing data shown in Figure 5.

claim: The crystal structure of the αBCL2•Bcl-2 complex was determined at 2.1 Å resolution.
source: The crystal structure of the αBCL2•Bcl-2 complex at 2.1 Å resolution together with the αMCL1•Mcl-1 complex described above illuminate the structural basis for affinity and specificity achieved by both computational design and evolution.
evidence: This is experimental structural data deposited in the PDB.

claim: The binding mode of αBCL2 in the hydrophobic cleft of Bcl-2 differs significantly between the crystal structure and backbone-constrained design model with 4.0 Å RMSD.
source: For example, the binding mode of αBCL2 in the hydrophobic cleft of Bcl-2 differs significantly between the crystal structure and backbone-constrained design model; after Bcl-2 alignment, Cα backbones of the αBCL2 crystal and design models deviate by 4.0 Å RMSD (average amongst the two complexes observed in the asymmetric unit; Figure 6—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison of the design model to the crystal structure.

claim: αBCL2 expands the classic BH3 interface by 452 Å².
source: Like αMCL1, αBCL2 expands the classic BH3 interface by 452 Å2 (Figure 6—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from the crystal structure shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Permeabilized MEFs treated with each designed inhibitor induced cytochrome c release only in the cell line dependent on the corresponding target BCL2 protein.
source: Strikingly, permeabilized MEFs treated with each designed inhibitor induced cytochrome c release only in the cell line dependent on the corresponding target BCL2 protein.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: No cytochrome c release was observed in Bak-/-Bax-/- cells after inhibitor treatment, confirming that mitochondrial outer membrane permeability occurs specifically via the BCL2-regulated intrinsic pathway.
source: No cytochrome c release was observed in Bak-/-Bax-/- cells, confirming that mitochondrial outer membrane permeability following inhibitor treatment occurs specifically via the BCL2-regulated intrinsic pathway, as expected (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: αMCL1 caused a 90 ± 11% decrease in survival in Mcl-1-dependent MEFs in long-term colony survival assays.
source: Consistent with binding profiles and cytochrome c release data, large effects were only seen with αMCL1 in the Mcl-1-dependent line, causing a 90 ± 11% decrease in survival, and with αBFL1 in the Bfl-1-dependent line, causing a 85 ± 6% decrease in survival (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1A.

claim: αBFL1 caused a 85 ± 6% decrease in survival in Bfl-1-dependent MEFs in long-term colony survival assays.
source: Consistent with binding profiles and cytochrome c release data, large effects were only seen with αMCL1 in the Mcl-1-dependent line, causing a 90 ± 11% decrease in survival, and with αBFL1 in the Bfl-1-dependent line, causing a 85 ± 6% decrease in survival (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1A.

claim: HeLa cells are resistant to the expression of Noxa and ABT-737 independently, but are potently killed with the combination of Noxa with ABT-737.
source: Previous studies revealed that HeLa cells are resistant to the expression of Noxa (which targets Mcl-1 and Bfl-1) and ABT-737 (Bcl-2 and Bcl-xL) independently, but are potently killed with the combination of Noxa with ABT-737 (van Delft et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: The combination of αMCL1 with αBCL2 resulted in 29 ± 9% survival in wild-type HeLa cells.
source: More substantial cell death was induced by combinations of αMCL1 with αBCL2 (29 ± 9% survival) and αMCL1 with αBCLXL (38 ± 17%) than αBCL2 with αBCLXL (75 ± 7%).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: The combination of αMCL1 with αBCLXL resulted in 38 ± 17% survival in wild-type HeLa cells.
source: More substantial cell death was induced by combinations of αMCL1 with αBCL2 (29 ± 9% survival) and αMCL1 with αBCLXL (38 ± 17%) than αBCL2 with αBCLXL (75 ± 7%).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: The combination of αBCL2 with αBCLXL resulted in 75 ± 7% survival in wild-type HeLa cells.
source: More substantial cell death was induced by combinations of αMCL1 with αBCL2 (29 ± 9% survival) and αMCL1 with αBCLXL (38 ± 17%) than αBCL2 with αBCLXL (75 ± 7%).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: Mcl-1 plays a more crucial role in wild-type HeLa survival than Bcl-2 or Bcl-xL.
source: These data, and similar results in Mcl-1-overexpressing (Mcl-1+) HeLa cells, suggest that Mcl-1 plays a more crucial role in wild-type HeLa survival than Bcl-2 or Bcl-xL.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data on cell survival with different inhibitor combinations.

claim: In wild-type HeLa cells, Bim associated primarily with Mcl-1.
source: In wild-type HeLa cells, Bim associated primarily with Mcl-1.
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Introduction of αMCL1 resulted in displacement of Bim from Mcl-1, with modest compensatory sequestration of Bim by Bcl-2 in wild-type HeLa cells.
source: Introduction of αMCL1 resulted in displacement of Bim from Mcl-1, with modest compensatory sequestration of Bim by Bcl-2.
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Apoptotic resistance in melanoma is thought to act via Bfl-1.
source: Apoptotic resistance in melanoma is thought to act via Bfl-1 (Hind et al., 2015), and likewise in glioblastoma via Bcl-2 (Weller et al., 1995) and Bcl-xL (Nagane et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Apoptotic resistance in glioblastoma is thought to act via Bcl-2.
source: Apoptotic resistance in melanoma is thought to act via Bfl-1 (Hind et al., 2015), and likewise in glioblastoma via Bcl-2 (Weller et al., 1995) and Bcl-xL (Nagane et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Apoptotic resistance in glioblastoma is thought to act via Bcl-xL.
source: Apoptotic resistance in melanoma is thought to act via Bfl-1 (Hind et al., 2015), and likewise in glioblastoma via Bcl-2 (Weller et al., 1995) and Bcl-xL (Nagane et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Oncogenic EGFR mutations in glioblastoma are associated with apoptotic resistance via increased Bcl-xL expression.
source: Further, oncogenic EGFR mutations in glioblastoma are associated with apoptotic resistance via increased Bcl-xL expression (Latha et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: LOX-IMVI melanoma cells were sensitive to double combinations that included αMCL1 and triple combinations.
source: While SK-MEL-5 were overall more resistant to apoptosis, LOX-IMVI melanoma cells were sensitive to double combinations that included αMCL1 and triple combinations (Figure 8A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: Mcl-1 plays a more critical role in survival than Bfl-1 in LOX-IMVI melanoma cells.
source: αBFL1 with αBCL2 or αBCLXL had less effect, indicating that Mcl-1 plays a more critical role in survival than Bfl-1 in LOX-IMVI, in contrast to mRNA profiling suggesting the opposite (Hind et al., 2015).
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data on cell survival with different inhibitor combinations.

claim: In previous studies, colon cancers showed a variable response to small-molecule-mediated Bcl-xL inhibition.
source: In previous studies, colon cancers showed a variable response to small-molecule-mediated Bcl-xL inhibition, and RNAi experiments identified Mcl-1 as a resistance factor (Zhang et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: RNAi experiments identified Mcl-1 as a resistance factor in colon cancers.
source: In previous studies, colon cancers showed a variable response to small-molecule-mediated Bcl-xL inhibition, and RNAi experiments identified Mcl-1 as a resistance factor (Zhang et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: SW48 cells showed greater than a 50% decrease in viability after treatment with A-1331852.
source: Inhibiting a single pro-survival homolog had little effect on short-term survival; only SW48 cells showed greater than a 50% decrease in viability after treatment with A-1331852, consistent with a previous study showing SW48 is sensitive to Bcl-xL inhibition (Zhang et al., 2015; Figure 9A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 9A.

claim: Combined inhibition of both Mcl-1 and Bcl-xL caused nearly complete cell death after 24 hr in all colon cancers except HCT-116.
source: Combined inhibition of both Mcl-1 and Bcl-xL caused nearly complete cell death after 24 hr in all colon cancers except HCT-116; further analyses showed that αMCL1-mediated Mcl-1 inhibition strongly sensitizes most colon cancers to A-1331852 (and to a lesser extent ABT-263), with a 4.6-fold or greater decrease in EC50 values observed in all cell lines except HCT-116 (Figure 9—figure supplement 1A–B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 9 and Figure 9—figure supplement 1.

claim: αMCL1-mediated Mcl-1 inhibition strongly sensitizes most colon cancers to A-1331852 with a 4.6-fold or greater decrease in EC50 values observed in all cell lines except HCT-116.
source: Combined inhibition of both Mcl-1 and Bcl-xL caused nearly complete cell death after 24 hr in all colon cancers except HCT-116; further analyses showed that αMCL1-mediated Mcl-1 inhibition strongly sensitizes most colon cancers to A-1331852 (and to a lesser extent ABT-263), with a 4.6-fold or greater decrease in EC50 values observed in all cell lines except HCT-116 (Figure 9—figure supplement 1A–B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 9—figure supplement 1A–B.

claim: αBFL1 caused a 63 ± 4% decrease in RKO cell survival in long-term survival assays.
source: In long-term survival assays, αMCL1 had negligible effect, but remarkably, αBFL1 caused a significant decrease in RKO cell survival (63 ± 4% decrease; Figure 9B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 9B.

claim: This work offers the first complete set of specific inhibitors for each of the six pro-survival BCL2 proteins.
source: This work offers the first complete set of specific inhibitors for each of the six pro-survival BCL2 proteins, including the first reported specific inhibitors for Bcl-w and Bcl-B.
evidence: This is a statement about the novelty of the work.

claim: This work includes the first reported specific inhibitors for Bcl-w and Bcl-B.
source: This work offers the first complete set of specific inhibitors for each of the six pro-survival BCL2 proteins, including the first reported specific inhibitors for Bcl-w and Bcl-B.
evidence: This is a statement about the novelty of the work.

claim: The designed inhibitors exhibit greater specificity than small molecule alternatives in many cases.
source: Our designed inhibitors exhibit greater specificity and in many cases higher affinity than small molecule alternatives, and have advantages unique to their protein composition.
evidence: This is supported by comparison of binding data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1H.

claim: The designed inhibitors exhibit higher affinity than small molecule alternatives in many cases.
source: Our designed inhibitors exhibit greater specificity and in many cases higher affinity than small molecule alternatives, and have advantages unique to their protein composition.
evidence: This is supported by comparison of binding data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1H.

claim: The designed proteins can be genetically encoded, enabling spatial and temporal control of expression.
source: The designed protein inhibitors can be genetically encoded, enabling spatial and temporal control of expression, and have distinct advantages over broadly eliminating the target BCL2 protein using CRISPR- or RNAi-mediated knockdown or knockout.
evidence: This is a general property of protein-based tools.

claim: Specific inhibitors cause the redistribution of Bim.
source: The designs can be used to probe mechanism; we show that specific inhibitors cause the redistribution of a representative BOP, Bim, and the approach can be used to probe other BOPs and compare 'mode 1' versus 'mode 2' inhibition of apoptosis (Llambi et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Bcl-xL is thought to interact with p53 at a site opposite the BH3-binding groove.
source: The designed proteins can also be used to distinguish interactions at sites other than the BH3-binding groove; for example, Bcl-xL is thought to interact with p53 at a site opposite the BH3-binding groove (Petros et al., 2004), and Bcl-2 is reported to interact with the IP3 receptor in the endoplasmic reticulum via Bcl-2's BH4-domain (Rong et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Bcl-2 is reported to interact with the IP3 receptor in the endoplasmic reticulum via Bcl-2's BH4-domain.
source: The designed proteins can also be used to distinguish interactions at sites other than the BH3-binding groove; for example, Bcl-xL is thought to interact with p53 at a site opposite the BH3-binding groove (Petros et al., 2004), and Bcl-2 is reported to interact with the IP3 receptor in the endoplasmic reticulum via Bcl-2's BH4-domain (Rong et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: The computational design calculations using BINDI as a starting point enabled achievement of high specificity and affinity immediately following design for Mcl-1 and Bcl-2.
source: Our computational design calculations using the stable de novo designed protein BINDI as a starting point enabled us to achieve, in the cases of Mcl-1 and Bcl-2, high specificity and affinity immediately following design, and in the cases of Bcl-xL, Bcl-w, Bfl-1 and Bcl-B, superior starting points for optimization compared to a single, pan-specific construct.
evidence: This is supported by the experimental binding data in Figure 2.

claim: The computational design calculations provided superior starting points for optimization compared to a single, pan-specific construct for Bcl-xL, Bcl-w, Bfl-1 and Bcl-B.

claim: High affinity and specificity protein inhibitors can be designed for each member of a closely-knit protein family.
source: More generally, computationally designed inhibitors enable the investigation of the biological roles of specific protein interactions with the high spatio-temporal control that can be achieved with tissue-specific and inducible promoters. Competing approaches offer less control. The distribution of small molecules is difficult to spatially or temporally control in vivo, and broadly eliminating the protein of interest with CRISPR or RNAi cannot probe interactions with a specific interface or capture mechanistic intricacies. This work demonstrates that high affinity and specificity protein inhibitors can be designed for each member of a closely-knit protein family, providing a unique opportunity to probe the importance of individual protein interactions.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the successful design of six specific inhibitors for the BCL2 family.
